messages.author: 23b384a0d94b9b78
messages.subject: Model fitting
parts:
Hi everyone, 
I am new to SECR analysis and I am building models for leopards in certain protected areas in Southern India. I will eventually move on to other animals we have camera-trapped (wolves and jackals) in other regions. I was thinking of building an exhaustive list of models involving variations in lambda0 and sigma (using at least b, bk, t and T along with a covariate sex). However I saw Murray mentioning that building such an exhaustive list of models checking is not a good practice. Then what would you recommend for choosing appropriate models for a species?
FYI,  my current species of focus are long ranging (sigma value from suggest.buffer argument is about 3kms.) and it is known the sex of the individual influences their activity ranges. 

Regards,

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Model fitting
parts:
Obsessing over detection models is unattractive when they do not represent biologically inspired hypotheses (b, bk in your case, unless camera sites were baited) or are likely to have trivial effects on the estimates (t, T in your case). And an exhaustive list of models would be very long. Conversely, you make a case for sex-dependence of sigma and lambda0 (note these go together). So the advice is to think it through. That includes trying a longer-tailed detection function than the default halfnormal (e.g., HEX), because that allows for occasional long movements.
That's my 2 cents worth. Other opinions welcome.
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Model fitting
parts: You seem to be heading for 'hybrid' mixture models that allow for unknown-sex animals (see ?hcov and secr-finitemixtures.pdf). These are specified with the hcov argument of secr.fit (i.e. hcov = 'sex' where 'sex is a covariate name) AND model = list(lambda0~h2, sigma~h2). Compare a model with hcov='sex' and model=list(lambda0~1, sigma~1). (I'm assuming detectfn = 'HEX'; otherwise swap g0 for lambda0).

parts:
Hi Murray, 
I encountered a problem while making the capture history for running the hcov models. We had 87 animals out of which we could not identify the sex of 9 animals. The sex for these were coded as UID (unidentified). Before running the hcov models I changed UID to NA (missing values). But while making the capthist file I get an error that "line 239 does not have 5 elements"). That is the line from where the missing values start for the sex column. I am attaching my code below: 

##input trap file
trap.file<-read.csv(file.choose(), header = T)
export(trap.file, "trap_cu2020.txt")
##input capture file
cap.file<-read.csv(file.choose(), header = T)
cap.file$SEX<-ifelse(str_detect(cap.file$SEX, "UID"),NA, cap.file$SEX) #changing unidentified sexed individuals to NA

export(cap.file, "cap_cu2020.txt")
#cap file has blanks in place of UID

capthist<- read.capthist("cap_cu2020.txt","trap_cu2020.txt", detector = "proximity", binary.usage=T, skip=1,fmt= "trapID",noccasions=125, covnames = c("SEX"))

messages.subject: Re: Model fitting
parts: I'm not going to untangle your R data manipulation issue, but note "Missing values (NA) are used for individuals of unknown class. If hcov has more than two levels, all but the first two levels are converted to NA". So because the levels of your factor are 'f', 'm' and 'UID' in that order, UID will automatically be treated as NA, and no pre-processing is needed.
